sources.molar_mass: 2 × N 14.007 + O 15.999 g/mol: CIAAW abridged standard atomic weights 2024, https://www.ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm
sources.molar_heat_capacity: C_v at 298.15 K = C_p − R = 38.617 − 8.314 J/(mol·K). C_p of N2O(g) at 298.15 K: NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, table N-026, https://janaf.nist.gov/tables/N-026.html. R: CODATA 2018, 8.314462618 J/(mol·K)
sources.phase: NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69), Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems, nitrous oxide: boiling_point is the saturation temperature at 101.325 kPa, and latent_heat_vaporization the vapour minus liquid enthalpy there, 16.4732 kJ/mol, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Load&ID=C10024972&Type=SatT&Digits=6&PLow=0.101325&PHigh=0.101325&PInc=0&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm. melting_point is the triple-point temperature (at 87.8 kPa), the lowest saturation temperature in the same data, which the melting point at 101.325 kPa differs from by under 0.1 K. latent_heat_fusion: 6.5 kJ/mol at 182.4 K, Atake and Chihara (1974), NIST Chemistry WebBook phase change data, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C10024972&Mask=4
